operator_casefile.project_type: PSP-3000 UMD read-failure repair triage with safe, unpowered inspection planning
functional_subsystems: UMD drive mechanical loading and spindle mechanism
UMD drive flex ribbon and board-side connector
Mainboard power, control, and drive-interface circuitry
Front case, screen, and internal access layers

decision_tree.next_action: Reject the HS catalog recommendation of a usb_fume_extractor.
decision_tree.purpose: The proposed airflow-controller demo is unrelated to PSP UMD diagnosis, has no stated role in the device, and lacks controller, actuator, runtime, dimensional, mechanical, and electrical evidence.

decision_tree.next_action: Record the exact PSP-3000 subrevision, visible damage, prior repair history, disc behavior, and whether the failure is intermittent before purchasing parts.
decision_tree.purpose: Subrevision and failure-history evidence are missing; the supplied compatibility claim covers PSP 2000 and PSP 300x variants but does not establish exact compatibility for this unit.

decision_tree.next_action: Perform only external, unpowered inspection: inspect the UMD door, spindle area visible through the opening, foreign material, cracked plastic, bent guides, and disc-label or hub damage.
decision_tree.purpose: Separate obvious media, contamination, and mechanical obstruction hypotheses without applying power.

decision_tree.next_action: Compare the reported symptom against controlled observations already available, such as whether the disc is recognized, spins, makes abnormal noises, or fails only with one disc; do not create new powered observations under the stated constraint.
decision_tree.purpose: Rank media, switch, connector, mechanical, optical, and board hypotheses without treating the drive as confirmed faulty.

decision_tree.next_action: If disassembly is authorized, shut down completely, disconnect external power, remove the removable battery first, and keep the battery isolated before opening the case.
decision_tree.purpose: Reduce short-circuit and accidental-power risks before accessing the drive; the supplied repair guidance identifies battery removal as part of UMD replacement.

decision_tree.next_action: Document screw locations and cable routing, then remove the front case and screen/ribbon access layers only as needed to reach the UMD drive; release ribbon connectors by their locking mechanisms rather than pulling on cables.
decision_tree.purpose: The supplied iFixit PSP-300x claim states that replacement requires front-case, screen/ribbon, and drive access and is substantially invasive.

decision_tree.next_action: Inspect and photograph the UMD drive ribbon, connector contacts, latch, seating, corrosion, torn flex, and board-side damage before disturbing them; reseat only if the connector and flex are visibly intact.
decision_tree.purpose: Distinguish connector or flex faults from a drive fault while preserving evidence and avoiding unnecessary replacement.

decision_tree.next_action: Inspect the lid/switch actuator and mechanical linkage for misalignment or breakage without bypassing the switch or applying power.
decision_tree.purpose: A lid-detection fault can mimic a drive or media failure; an open-powered laser or drive test is prohibited.

decision_tree.next_action: Do not authorize a paid UMD-drive replacement until media, lid-switch, connector/flex, and obvious mechanical causes have been assessed and exact part compatibility is verified.
decision_tree.purpose: The supplied claims do not confirm that this specific PSP-3000 subrevision has a failed drive or that a particular replacement listing is exact.

compatible_parts_or_requirements: A replacement UMD drive is only a candidate: the supplied product claim lists compatibility with PSP 2000 and PSP 300x variants, but exact PSP-3000 subrevision compatibility remains unverified.

Use the device's existing drive flex and connector only after visual inspection confirms matching geometry, intact contacts, and a functional locking mechanism; no substitute flex or connector is authorized without exact verification.
Use a known-good, undamaged UMD only if a later approved powered diagnostic permits it; no disc-based conclusion can be made under the current no-power-test constraint.

Required repair conditions: removable battery isolated before opening, documented screw and cable locations, ESD-aware handling, suitable precision drivers, nonmetallic inspection tools where practical, and no powered laser or open-drive test.
Do not select a replacement drive by appearance alone; verify exact model, connector arrangement, mechanical geometry, and subrevision fit against the device and the supplier's return policy.
build_or_repair_sequence: 1. Freeze the current state in the repair record: PSP-3000 identification, subrevision evidence, symptom description, known disc history, prior repairs, visible damage, and authorization limits.
2. Externally inspect the UMD door, disc path, spindle opening, and visible mechanism with the device unpowered.
3. Remove external power and remove the battery before any case opening; keep the battery disconnected throughout inspection.
4. Photograph the exterior, screw locations, cable routing, screen/ribbon connections, UMD drive flex, connector latch, and switch linkage before removal.
5. Follow the supplied PSP-300x repair guidance through front-case and screen/ribbon access only as far as necessary to inspect the drive.
6. Inspect the drive flex and both connector interfaces for tears, contamination, corrosion, lifted contacts, damaged latch parts, or poor seating; document findings before reseating.
7. Inspect the UMD switch actuator and drive mechanics for obstruction, broken guides, displaced springs, or cracked mounts; do not bypass the switch.
8. Stop and route to salvage if the fault is limited to a recoverable connector, flex seating issue, contamination, or mechanical obstruction and the repair can be completed without unverified parts.
9. Route to replacement evaluation only if evidence implicates the drive and an exact compatible part is verified; otherwise retain the original drive and defer purchase.
10. Reassemble in reverse order with all ribbons fully latched and the battery remaining isolated until the enclosure and drive are secured.
11. Perform only the acceptance checks permitted by the owner and safety constraints; no open-powered laser or drive test is allowed.
critical_technical_unknowns: Exact PSP-3000 subrevision and whether its drive interfaces match the cited PSP 2000/300x replacement listing.
Whether the failure affects all discs or only one disc, and whether any prior controlled symptom observation exists.
Whether the disc is recognized, spins, fails to spin, makes abnormal noises, or produces an error.
Condition and alignment of the UMD lid switch and actuator.
Condition of the UMD flex ribbon, connector contacts, connector latch, and mainboard-side interface.
Presence of contamination, foreign objects, cracked guides, spindle damage, or mechanical binding.
Whether the optical pickup, spindle motor, drive controller, or mainboard circuitry is actually faulty; drive failure is not confirmed.
Availability of an exact-match replacement drive, return option, donor unit, and qualified repair labor.
Permitted post-repair power and media testing; the current constraint explicitly disallows power-on tests.
Repair time, labor rate, parts price, shipping, return cost, and budget limit.
validation_plan: Verify that the repair record identifies the PSP-3000 subrevision and preserves before-disassembly photographs and observations.
Verify that the battery was removed before case opening and that no powered inspection occurred with the drive exposed.
Verify that the drive flex and connector latch are intact, correctly seated, and free of documented contamination or damage.
Verify that the UMD switch linkage and visible mechanical path are correctly positioned and unobstructed.

If power testing later becomes authorized, test only after complete reassembly and use a known-good disc plus the reported disc; record recognition, spin-up, read stability, unusual noise, and repeatability.
Reject any validation procedure requiring an open-powered laser or drive test.
Acceptance cannot be declared until an approved post-repair functional test is defined; under the current no-power constraint, only unpowered inspection results can be recorded.
deliverable_gaps: No symptom-level evidence distinguishing media, switch, connector, mechanical, optical, or board faults.
No authorized post-repair powered acceptance procedure.
No verified exact replacement part number or supplier evidence for this unit.
No time and cost figures; labor, parts, shipping, tools, donor availability, and budget are unknown.
No confirmed baseline revision or prior repair state.
The supplied HS catalog metadata is for a robot/airflow-controller concept and is irrelevant to this PSP repair.

catalog_compatibility_gate.rationale: Device project does not explicitly approve this catalog build. LLM confidence cannot substitute for device compatibility evidence.
